titulo: B1 simulado: listening, reading, grammar, speaking and writing: Speaking and writing tasks, with a self-check list

aula.titulo: B1 simulado: listening, reading, grammar, speaking and writing
aula.objetivo: Check your B1 level honestly in four sessions: understand a text and a conversation, apply grammar and vocabulary, plan and judge a written and a spoken task with a self-check list, and solve a scored mixed set of 24 items. The simulado is Linvuu's own self-assessment and is not equivalent to any external exam.

sessao.titulo: Speaking and writing tasks, with a self-check list

blocos.titulo: How to prepare, write and speak, and how to judge yourself
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: PLAN. Spend two minutes before you begin: who am I writing to or talking to, what is the purpose, which three points will I cover? STEP 2: STRUCTURE. A formal e-mail has a subject, a greeting («Prezada senhora» / «Prezado senhor»), the reason («Escrevo para...»), the request («Gostaria de saber...»), a closing («Fico à disposição. Atenciosamente,»). A spoken monologue has an opening, two or three points with examples, and a closing. STEP 3: VARY the language: use at least one hypothesis, one subjunctive, one past with the perfeito and the imperfeito, and four connectors («além disso», «no entanto», «portanto», «apesar de»). STEP 4: KEEP SPEAKING. If a word is missing, paraphrase («é uma coisa que serve para...»); if you need time, say «deixa eu pensar»; if you lose the thread, say «ou seja...» and restart. STEP 5: CHECK. After writing, reread once for tenses, agreement, accents and the grave accent «à»; after speaking, listen to your recording and use the list below. The list is a self-assessment tool by Linvuu; it is not a score from an external examiner and it is not equivalent to any external exam.

tabela.ask_yourself: Did I answer every point asked, and did I keep to the topic?
Is there an opening, a development and a closing? Did I use at least four connectors?
Did I choose the right past tense, and use at least one subjunctive and one hypothesis correctly?
Do gender, number and verb endings agree? Did I use «de», «em», «a/à» correctly?
Is it consistent: «o senhor» with formal forms, or «você» with neutral ones, no slang in a formal text?
Did I vary the words and avoid English words and false friends?
Did I paraphrase, ask for repetition or buy time instead of stopping?
Are the nasals, the r, the final l and tch/dj before i clear enough to be understood?

blocos.enunciado: WRITING TASK (about 100 to 120 words, 8 minutes, no dictionary first). You live in Curitiba and want to take an evening Portuguese course. Write a formal e-mail to the school: say who you are, ask about price, start date and documents, say when you are available, and close politely. Then check yourself with the list above and compare with the model.
blocos.exemplo: Assunto: Informações sobre o curso noturno de português. Prezada senhora, meu nome é Michael Brown e moro em Curitiba há um ano. Estou escrevendo para pedir informações sobre o curso de português à noite. Gostaria de saber quanto custa, quando começa a próxima turma e quais documentos preciso levar. Além disso, pode me dizer se há aulas de conversação? Trabalho até as seis, por isso preciso de um horário depois das sete. Caso haja vagas, gostaria de fazer a matrícula ainda este mês. Fico à disposição e agradeço desde já a atenção. Atenciosamente, Michael Brown.

blocos.enunciado: SPEAKING TASK (about 2 minutes, record yourself). Talk about "a day I will remember": what happened (perfeito), how the place and the people were (imperfeito), something that had already happened before (mais-que-perfeito), and what you would do differently (hypothesis with «se»). Then answer three questions aloud: «Por que você estuda português?», «O que você faria se morasse um ano no Brasil?», «O que você espera do futuro?». Listen to the recording and judge yourself with the list.
blocos.exemplo: Model opening: «Vou contar sobre o dia em que cheguei ao Brasil. Era uma manhã de chuva e eu estava nervoso, porque nunca tinha viajado sozinho. No aeroporto, uma funcionária me ajudou, embora eu falasse muito pouco. Se eu tivesse estudado mais antes de viajar, teria entendido melhor. Mesmo assim, foi um dia inesquecível...»

blocos.enunciado: Choose one topic you know well (your work, your city, your family). Think of five words and two connectors that you could use to talk about it for two minutes. Say them aloud.
